blocks.text:
After breakfast, we head to the Argentine side of the falls. The national park has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

An ecological train runs through the park. It passes through tropical forest and stops at the start of the walking trails. From there, bridges and paths lead towards the water, allowing you to see the falls at very close range.

The route follows approximately 1700 metres of bridges and walkways. Here, you see the cascades from below. They include Álvar Núñez, Elenita, Lanusse and El Salto Bossetti, which falls in an almost unbroken wall of water.

**Duration:** 1 hour 45 minutes.  
**Difficulty:** moderate.
